answers.note: Strong concrete-pictorial-abstract sequence with a whiteboard check and clear follow-up, but the challenge missing-digit item is printed with visible muddled self-correction (4_ + 38 = 73 is impossible) before being fixed.
Accurate, well-timed lesson with block modelling, a diagnostic hinge question and a clear reteach threshold, though the practice is mostly plain sums with only one word problem for variety.

Excellent pack: concrete-pictorial-abstract modelling, diagnostic hinge questions with a specific response plan, and practice that moves from an exchange/no-exchange sort through faded examples to reasoning, all with correct maths.

Clear PEEL scaffold and an 8-mark task with model paragraph, but the Yale setting is never stated, the teacher model comes after students have already written, and the ethics MCQ is ambiguous (deception and right to withdraw are both defensible).

Outstanding explicit teaching of evaluation through a four-step chain with I do/we do/you do and a broken model to repair, but no actual AQA exam question is set for students, only a reference to the 16-mark format.
Accurate procedure and findings, a staged evaluation workshop (model, card sort, build) and an AQA-style 6-mark question with a peer-check checklist make it fully meet every criterion.

Logical sequence with weekly retrieval starters, but safety covers only short circuits with no mention of mains danger, the baseline is a single oral question, and 'bulbs share the electricity' reinforces a used-up misconception.
Strong baseline torch drawing, safety and end quiz, but Week 1 has no hands-on kit activity and the Week 4 and 5 starters introduce new content rather than retrieving earlier learning.

Thorough, well-sequenced unit with kit-based practicals every week, spaced retrieval starters, a matched before/after assessment and accurate Year 4 pitch including clear mains and short-circuit safety.
